description: RDT SQL Code Standards for automated validation

format.name: Line Breaker
format.description: Use Windows line break (CRLF), no Unix line break (LF)

format.name: TAB Size
format.description: Use 3 spaces instead of TAB control

general.name: CREATE OR ALTER
general.description: Must use CREATE OR ALTER in SP scripts

general.name: TRY CATCH for Data Operations
general.description: All DELETE, UPDATE, INSERT, MERGE must be wrapped in BEGIN TRY...BEGIN CATCH

general.name: Schema Prefix
general.description: All table references must include schema prefix

general.name: ROWLOCK for Updates
general.description: Must add WITH (ROWLOCK) when updating data

general.name: TRY_CAST for Type Conversion
general.description: Must use TRY_CAST for data type conversion, avoid implicit conversion

general.name: GRANT Permission
general.description: Grant execution permission to NSQL role at end of SP/function scripts

general.name: Unique Error Numbers
general.description: Each error number must be unique in the system

general.name: NOLOCK for Queries
general.description: Add WITH (NOLOCK) to all query statements unless specific reason

general.name: GO Statement
general.description: GO statement must be appended to end of CREATE PROCEDURE and GRANT Permission

extendedScreen.name: ExtScnSP Config Name
extendedScreen.description: RDT extended screen configuration must be named ExtScnSP

extendedScreen.name: Step_99 Label
extendedScreen.description: Extended screen section step label must be Step_99

extendedScreen.name: Unified Variable Names
extendedScreen.description: Use standard variable names in extended screen SPs

variables.@nStep: Step value passed to extended screen SP
variables.@nScn: Screen value passed to extended screen SP
variables.@nAfterStep: Next step value returned to main SP
variables.@nAfterScn: Next screen value returned to main SP
variables.@nPreStep: Previous step that calls extended screen SP
variables.@nPreScn: Previous screen that calls extended screen SP

bestPractice.name: Query Performance
bestPractice.description: Hit primary key or index in conditions to avoid long queries
guidelines: Use indexed columns in WHERE clause

bestPractice.name: Primary Key for Updates
bestPractice.description: Use primary keys to update or delete data whenever possible

bestPractice.name: Table Variables for Batch Operations
bestPractice.description: Use table variables or temp tables for batch updates/deletes instead of complex WHERE clauses
guidelines: Collect target records into table variable first
Loop through table variable to process in batches
Use EXISTS with table variable to limit UPDATE/DELETE scope
Avoid long-running locks on large tables

example.good: UPDATE dbo.Table WITH(ROWLOCK) SET Col=@Val WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM @tTableVar TV WHERE TV.Key = Table.Key)
example.bad: UPDATE dbo.Table SET Col=@Val WHERE ComplexCondition1 AND ComplexCondition2 AND EXISTS(...)

bestPractice.name: Minimal Transactions
bestPractice.description: Only include necessary operations in transactions

bestPractice.name: Comments for Complex Logic
bestPractice.description: Add comments to help others understand complex logic
